_sources.resolution: reports/w6_resolution_diagnosis.json (MAE, naive MAE, n_test, bucket delta; CI-guarded) + reports/resolution_results.json (ci_coverage only; gitignored, regenerated by scripts/09_train_resolution.py, NOT CI-guarded) + docs/architecture/adr/0009,0025
_sources.conformal: reports/cqr_conformal_adjustments_v2.snapshot.json (byte-identical copy of data/models/cqr_conformal_adjustments_v2.json, the file served; sha256 pinned by data/models/MANIFEST.sha256) + scripts/analysis_served_k8s_metrics.py + reports/served_k8s_metrics.json + docs/architecture/adr/0010
_sources.resolution_served: scripts/build_resolution_served_block.py from reports/served_k8s_metrics.json + reports/vscode_naive_serving_eval.json + reports/d7_resolution_before_after.json + data/models/MANIFEST.sha256 + docs/architecture/adr/0064

leakage.removal_reason: Assigned post-creation (not available at triage time); corr=0.595 with log(resolution_hours), fills 6.9% on fast issues vs 93.1% on slow — pure leakage.

prior_metrics_invalidated.note: These metrics were computed on a broken closed_at temporal split where test issues were closed before some train issues were created. Retracted. See ADR-0009.

k8s.ci_coverage_metric: raw Q10-Q90 resolution interval (no CQR), nominal 80%, on the full test split (n_test); NOT the CQR conformal coverage in section 5

vscode.note: LightGBM underperforms naive on vscode because there is no creation-time signal that predicts resolution time for this repo. The system detects this at the repo level (bucket classifier accuracy −22.08pp vs naive, 95% CI [−25.81, −18.02] — ADR-0025; the −70.5% figure above is the separate POINT-regression MAE degradation, not the bucket model's) and surfaces a badge to the user rather than presenting a prediction that is worse than the baseline.
vscode.ci_coverage_metric: raw Q10-Q90 resolution interval (no CQR), nominal 80%, on the full test split (n_test); NOT the CQR conformal coverage in section 5

deployment.gap_disclosure: resolution_predictor_{slug}.pkl was retrained on the corrected created_at split and uploaded to GCS on 2026-06-19, but engineer_features() also reads data/processed/{slug}_temporal_train.parquet at inference time for historical-aggregate features, and that companion file was NOT re-uploaded — GCS retained the pre-ADR-0009 parquet (uploaded 2026-05-02). MANIFEST.sha256 only covered data/models/*, so nothing detected the mismatch. The Cloud Run revisions serving from 2026-06-19 06:00 UTC through 2026-06-20 17:41 UTC served the corrected model weights joined against pre-fix training data — an internally inconsistent hybrid, not simply the old leaky behavior. See ADR-0009 'Deployment Correction' for full detail including measured before/after values on live /triage.

leakage.honest_metrics_status: historical: the 2026-05-30 retrain scored on the created_at split (k8s n=1498, vscode n=616). NOT what production serves today; see resolution_served (ADR-0064).

calibration.method: single shared temperature T on the one-vs-rest sigmoid logits of the 47-class multi-label TF-IDF+LR classifier (ADR-0036, ADR-0057); argmax-preserving, so accuracy is unchanged by calibration
calibration.classifier: 47-class multi-label OvR retrain, promoted locally 2026-09-04 (ADR-0057), published to GCS 2026-09-23 (MANIFEST.sha256, commit 6ae3e84)
calibration.ece_test_definition: top-1 confidence ECE (ADR-0004 calibration_analysis) on data/processed/{repo}_classifier_test.parquet, the fresh test split (n=423 vscode / n=671 k8s); reports/multilabel_classifier_final_training.json
calibration.ece_eval_set_definition: same ECE (n_bins=5) on the 64-issue gold eval set (eval/eval_set.jsonl, n=11 vscode / n=53 k8s); eval/test_invariants.py _RECORDED_ECE, ADR-0058. Small n: noisy, not comparable to ece_test
calibration.val_ece_note: Pre/post-calibration validation-split ECE was not recorded for the retrained classifier (only the test-split result in reports/multilabel_classifier_final_training.json), so those two columns are shown as unavailable rather than carried over from the retired classifier.

previous_classifier.description: Retired 28-class (vscode) / 35-class (k8s) single-label softmax classifier, temperature-scaled (ADR-0004). Replaced by the 47-class retrain (GCS 2026-09-23). History only; NOT the production classifier.
previous_classifier.deployment_gap_disclosure: The calibrated classifier pkl was fitted on 2026-05-19 but the GCS artifact was not updated at that time. Production served the UNCALIBRATED classifier from approximately 2026-05-02 to 2026-06-19. The ece_test values below (0.138/0.156) were accurate for the calibrated model but were NOT what production was serving during that period.
previous_classifier.isotonic_note: Isotonic calibration tested (vscode test ECE 0.072, k8s 0.026) but not shipped — accuracy CIs overlapped zero and temperature scaling is simpler/more interpretable.

judge.baseline_note: Current baseline, copied from reports/eval_baseline.json (schema v2) by hand and guarded by tests/test_api.py::test_eval_summary_judge_block_matches_committed_baseline. Local qwen3:8b judge (ADR-0019) on the train-decontaminated gold set (ADR-0018). Scores from earlier judges (llama-3.3-70b-versatile, command-a-03-2025) were measured on a different n=60 set and are not comparable; they were removed from this file on 2026-10-05 and remain in git history.

reranker.phase1_verdict: Mixed — k8s gain, vscode regression. Proceeded to robustness test.
reranker.phase2_verdict: CI crosses zero — the Phase 1 +6pp k8s result was a false positive at n=100. Reranker rejected. BGE FAISS k=20 baseline shipped.
reranker.slates_note: 8 cross-encoder candidates across 2 slates (general-purpose + duplicate/STS models); all failed or showed mixed/negative results before bge-v2-m3 robustness test.

conformal.caveats: Marginal (not conditional) coverage; assumes exchangeability. vscode train(2015-16)/test(2026, 7-day window) violates this — report empirical coverage, not theoretical guarantee.

kubernetes/kubernetes.calibration_split: 30/70 of the ADR-0041 re-split test (897 cal / 2095 true-test), calibrated on served-path features (cqr_conformal_adjustments_v2.json)

microsoft/vscode.calibration_split: 40/60 of test (246 cal / 370 true-test), the split production loads (loader.py); 30/70 also computed, see split_sensitivity
microsoft/vscode.exchangeability_note: train 2015-10-13..2016-04-05, test 2026-04-21..2026-04-27 (7-day window). Temporal regime gap violates exchangeability; 74.6% empirical coverage vs 80% target is the honest outcome.

point_estimate.definition: median(resolution_hours of the training set) / 24, the same naive baseline the published comparison uses
point_estimate.why: The learned point estimate has a worse median absolute error than the training-window median in both repos; it is not served. The learned parts that stay are the k8s bucket classifier and the conformal intervals.

kubernetes/kubernetes.window: ADR-0041 re-split temporal test, served path through _collect_signals

bucket.served: naive majority prior (classifier not trusted, ADR-0025)

interval.served: model relative width re-centred on the median + stored CQR Q
interval.caveat: single 7-day window; train median 3.84 d vs test median 0.049 d; coverage is a measurement, not a guarantee
